title: Dock a Nintendo Switch: lower the console straight down its dock's slot until its port seats on the hidden USB-C plug
instruction: Lower the console into its dock, its screen facing the way the dock's front faces, so it connects, then let go.
context: Most people with a Nintendo Switch put it back in its dock to play on the TV or to charge it; Nintendo has sold 157.2 million Switch consoles. Nintendo's step is "Position the console so that the console screen faces in the same direction as the front panel on the dock", then insert it: the console goes straight down the slot until the USB-C plug at the bottom, out of sight, enters the port on its lower edge. The plug is an 8.25 x 2.4 mm tongue and the port's 8.34 x 2.56 mm opening clears it by under 0.1 mm a side (USB Type-C), so the 242 mm wide, 420 g console has to come down upright and centred. Tilted or off to one side, the port lands beside the plug and the console rests unconnected: nothing shows on the TV and it does not charge. Dropped in, it strikes the plug instead of being lowered onto it. Unlike pushing a held plug into a visible port, here the port is on the device, the plug hidden. A Switch OLED with both Joy-Con attached lies screen down on a rest in front of its dock.
setup: Centimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the bench top. A Nintendo Switch OLED dock with LAN port, 103.7 mm high, 174 mm long, 47.4 mm deep and 286 g (ChargerLAB's measurement; Nintendo: about 4.1 x 6.9 x 2.0 in), stands upright on the bench centred at (30, -10), its 174 mm length along y, its front toward the robot. Its slot opens in its top, 16 mm wide (x) and 45 mm deep, 9 mm behind the front face, and runs the whole length along y; at the middle of the slot's floor stands a USB-C plug, 8.25 x 2.4 mm (USB Type-C plug size), 6.5 mm tall, with a chamfered tip, rigid (the real one sits on springs). Two fixed rest blocks, 150 mm high and 66 x 30 mm (a staging rest, standing in for the hand or shelf the console comes from), stand at (47, -20) and (47, 0), one under each Joy-Con, their tops covered with a microfibre cloth. A Nintendo Switch OLED model with both Joy-Con attached (Nintendo: 102 x 242 x 13.9 mm; 420 g) lies on them screen down, its screen glass (154.9 x 87.2 mm, a 7.4 mm bezel at the top and lower edges) touching nothing, centred at (46, -10), its 242 mm width along y and its port, a pocket 9.25 x 3.4 mm and 6.6 mm deep in the middle of its lower edge, toward the robot's far side (+x). Its top edge overhangs the blocks by 30 mm toward the robot, so each hand's jaws can close across the edge's 13.9 mm thickness at a Joy-Con end, 104 mm either side of the middle (the glass ends 77 mm out). Real trial: protect the screen with its own film or a microfibre sleeve, and the gripper pads with nitrile finger cots or a soft pad cover. In the simulator the pads are plain and nothing is soft; the demo grips only the frame at the Joy-Con ends, never the glass, and a check counts every step a finger point is over the glass (0 in the demo). Seated, the console stands upright in the slot, screen toward the robot, its port fully on the plug; while the plug is in the port it resists with up to 8 N of friction, inside USB Type-C's 5 to 20 N mating force range, so the console's own 4.1 N weight does not seat it and the hands push the rest. Estimates, with ranges and real checks in the README: the slot's 16 mm width (range 14.5 to 17; the console is 13.9 mm) and 45 mm depth, the plug's height, the pocket's 0.5 mm a side (the real receptacle, 8.34 x 2.56 mm, is under 0.1 mm a side, but the real plug floats on springs) and the frictions (0.4). Nothing else is on the bench. Both arms start at their ready pose, grippers open; each hand takes one Joy-Con end of the console. For a real trial: the dock's AC adapter plugged in, an HDMI cable to a display, and the console awake; or watch the dock's LED.
scoring: Terms. Judged means the state at the end, once both grippers (fingers and housings) and every arm joint are at least 3 cm from the console and the console and the dock have been still for 1 s (real trial: from the trial video); a run not settled at its end scores 0, and a tier reached earlier and then undone does not count. In the slot: the console's lower edge, its middle and its lowest corner, at least 4 mm below the dock's rim and the middle of that edge, where the port is, over the opening, within the slot's 16 mm width and within 34 mm of the dock's middle along its length, so the 242 mm console spans the whole 174 mm dock with both Joy-Con past its ends; a console beside the dock, off to one end or past either end, is not in the slot (real trial: from the top camera's view, the console's lower edge inside the slot between the dock's ends). Seated: the port fully on the plug, to within 0.7 mm of its stop (real trial: the TV shows the console's picture, or the dock's LED lights; AC adapter, HDMI cable, display, console awake). Upright: within 2 degrees of the dock's own upright and square to its slot, its screen the way the dock's front panel faces (toward the robot) (real trial: a phone level app against the console's back, free, reading to 0.1 degree). Lowered: its port arrives on the plug slower than 0.25 m/s, the speed of a fall of about 3 mm, judged on every arrival of its lower edge at the plug's tip, onto the port or anywhere beside it along the edge, since it was last lifted 4 mm or more off the plug (real trial: a side phone video with the ruler stood behind the console's top edge; once both hands let go, the top edge falls no more than 3 mm before the console stops on the plug, and the hands then push it home; a console that falls further once let go is dropped). Tiers: 1.0 seated, upright and lowered; 0.5 upright within 5 degrees in the slot but not seated, or seated but dropped in; 0.25 in the slot but jammed tilted up to 15 degrees, or turned screen away from the robot; leaning further, it scores 0. Zeros that stick: the dock moved more than 2 cm or tipped more than 5 degrees (real trial: a masking-tape outline around its base and a ruler), or the console fallen off the bench. Free: which hand does what, the path, how long it takes, and lifting or turning the console on the way cost nothing by themselves. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. The run ends with success once 1.0 has held for 1 s.
run_limit: 1,200 steps (60 s at 20 Hz), about 2 times the 30 s scripted demo
reset_notes: The console screen down on its rest, top edge toward the robot; the dock at its mark. No seed changes the scene.
fidelity: Rigid boxes at published sizes: console 102 x 242 x 13.9 mm, 420 g; dock 103.7 x 174 x 47.4 mm, 286 g (measured), upright. Start: a staging rest of two 150 mm blocks (real: a hand or a shelf), so both hands reach the top edge over the dock. The plug's 8 N friction (USB Type-C: 5 to 20 N) is a force set each physics step between console and dock while the plug is in the port. Slot, pocket, frictions estimated; the real plug floats on springs, here rigid with a 0.5 mm pocket. Plain pads.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 in its 1,200 steps; demo: 1.0
